chunks: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a domesticated bird that came and entered the Haram, and he said:
"It is not to be taken nor touched, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:
'And whoever enters it shall be safe.'"

key_terms.آمِنًا: safe and secure under sanctuary protection
key_terms.أَهْلِيٍّ: domesticated; belonging to human habitation or ownership
key_terms.الْحَرَمَ: the Sacred Sanctuary in which special protections apply
key_terms.لَا يُؤْخَذُ: it is not to be seized or taken
key_terms.لَا يُمَسُّ: it is not to be touched or handled

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a domesticated bird that enters the Haram sanctuary?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a domesticated bird that enters the Haram: it is not to be taken or touched. The Imam عليه السلام supports this ruling by citing the Qur'anic principle that whoever enters the sanctuary is granted safety.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2367 - Muawiyah ibn Ammar asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a domesticated bird that entered the Sacred Sanctuary (Haram).
Imam (as) replied: "It should not be taken or touched because Allah (swt), the Almighty, says:
'And whoever enters it shall be safe.'"
